newsitem.title: USA: Oppenheimer Capital keeps partnership form.
newsitem.headline: Oppenheimer Capital keeps partnership form.

text.p: Oppenheimer Capital LP said on Wednesday that it voted to remain a publicly traded partnership, due to a new tax law that keeps it from paying corporate income taxes.

The Tax Relief Act of 1997 allows certain publicly traded partnerships to maintain partnership tax status that has a new 3.5 percent tax on trade and business revenue starting in calendar 1998, Oppenheimer said in a statement.
Previously, Oppenheimer would have lost its partnership status in January 1998, making it subject to costlier corporate taxes on its net income, it said.
